concept: Band portrait in a paper-mural studio
creativeDirection: Editorial studio photography: build one real photographed set around the strongest castable group, using the graphic sleeves as physical studio-surface motifs and small props rather than separate scenes.
scene: A purpose-built white studio set with one freestanding curved wall and bare floor, partly overpainted with bold torn-paper-style colour blocks and collage marks, where the cast group stands together as if caught during a stylised editorial shoot.

elements.element: the five clearly visible people from reference image 1 posed together with the front woman centred slightly forward, preserving their sleeve pose and styling
large torn-paper-style painted shapes across the curved studio wall, forming a bold yellow face-like arrangement without becoming a separate picture
a thin outlined zeppelin painted high across the wall with a few small biplane and star collage decals scattered nearby
a freestanding glossy sculptural lips-and-tongue sign leaning against the wall at floor level on the right
a small white flower emblem printed on a dark olive square floor mat under part of the group

coverSummaries.description: Five young adults pose closely together against a plain white studio background. In front, a woman with long dark hair stands with arms outstretched wearing a fuzzy cropped top and plaid skirt; around her are a bald woman at left, a short-haired blond man in a sleeveless jersey, a dark-haired man in profile behind them, a dark-haired man in a checkered cardigan, and a blonde woman at far right with her hands near her head. The image has a high-contrast, posterised photographic look.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: group of five young adults posed in a row
coverSummaries.people: six young adults posing shoulder to shoulder
coverSummaries.place: a plain white studio backdrop with no visible furniture or architectural features.

coverSummaries.description: A bold graphic illustration of a stylised human face fills most of the square, built from torn-paper-like shapes. The face is bright yellow with simplified dark purple features, a small red circular eye, green hair, and a red ear, set against jagged red, green, white, and dark blue blocks around the edges.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: stylised yellow face made of torn-paper shapes

coverSummaries.description: A dense collage-style design on an off-white background combines a large outlined zeppelin shape and many scattered small images and symbols. Visible elements include airships, vintage biplanes, butterflies, birds, circular portrait cutouts, a mouth with teeth, flowers, stars, abstract paint splashes, patterned circles, and assorted surreal fragments arranged across the surface.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: large outlined zeppelin amid a surreal collage

coverSummaries.description: A large cropped tongue-and-lips graphic dominates the right side on a plain white background. The lips are blue and the tongue has a smooth gradient shifting from yellow and orange at the bottom through red and purple to blue near the top, with white teeth visible above.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: large multicoloured tongue and lips symbol

coverSummaries.description: A simple centered white flower emblem with two leaves and a stem sits on a dark olive-green gradient background. The flower has black line details and a clean, logo-like appearance with soft shadowing behind it.

prompt: A real photographic studio set in 16:9, shot at eye level in a medium-wide frame with a slight diagonal view rather than straight-on symmetry; a curved white cyc wall meets a clean matte floor, the camera close enough for faces to read clearly. The five clearly visible people from reference image 1 are the only people present, standing together at their own scale in the near middle ground, preserving their sleeve pose, gaze, hair, and styling, with the front woman from reference image 1 slightly forward and the others grouped tightly around her. Behind and around them, the white studio wall is partly painted with bold torn-paper-style blocks derived from reference image 2, including a large yellow face-like arrangement with dark blue, red, and green shapes integrated as studio decoration rather than a separate artwork. High on the wall, include a thin outlined zeppelin and a few small scattered biplane and star collage decals from reference image 3. At floor level on the right, place a glossy freestanding multicoloured lips-and-tongue sign from reference image 4 leaning casually against the wall. Under one side of the group, place a dark olive square floor mat carrying the small white flower emblem from reference image 5. Clean editorial studio photography, physically plausible set build, sharp focus, no extra people, no text. Light the cast with a high softbox from one side and broad white bounce fill so every face is evenly legible and the colours stay clean and bright; crisp whites, saturated yellow, blue, red, and green accents, playful graphic energy with a polished contemporary music-blog feel. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 1 is cropped to the 5 people on that sleeve whose face is clearly visible - portray only those people and nobody else from it, and reference image 6 is an enlarged close-up of those same people - take their faces from reference image 6. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The only people anywhere in the image are the reference people named in the reference map, and of those only the ones whose faces are clearly visible in their reference. Add no one else: no extra band members, musicians, staff, bystanders, passers-by, crowd, audience, background or out-of-focus figures, and no hands, arms, legs, or shadows of unseen people. Never complete a person who is hidden, cropped, turned away, blurred, or only partly visible in a reference with an invented face or body - leave that person out entirely. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
